entities.summary: Bernat de Puigcercós (O.P.) was a Catalan Dominican friar who lived during the 14th century and served as general Inquisitor of the Crown of Aragon. He played a significant role in the prosecution of heresy in the region, particularly during the reign of King John I of Aragon. This period saw the implementation of the Edict of Expulsion, which led to the forced expulsion of Jews from the kingdom. De Puigcercós' actions had a lasting impact on the religious and social landscape of the region, shaping the trajectory of Catholicism in the Crown of Aragon. His legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Inquisition in the region until its abolition in the 19th century. The Catholic Church's efforts to suppress dissenting voices and maintain orthodoxy had far-reaching consequences, including the persecution of minority groups and the suppression of alternative religious practices. This legacy continues to be felt today, with ongoing debates about the role of religious authority and the balance between freedom of religion and national security.

entities.summary:
Bernat de Puigcercós (O.P.) was a Catalan Dominican friar who played a crucial role in the Inquisition during the 14th century. He was born in Girona, Catalonia, in 1300 and died in 1342. As general Inquisitor of the Crown of Aragon, Bernat de Puigcercós was responsible for rooting out heresy and enforcing Catholic orthodoxy.

His tenure as Inquisitor was marked by the persecution of Jews, Muslims, and other minority groups, as well as the forced conversion of many people to Christianity. The Inquisition also used torture and imprisonment as tools of coercion, and Bernat de Puigcercós was instrumental in implementing these measures.

Despite his significant role in the Inquisition, Bernat de Puigcercós is often overlooked in historical accounts. However, his legacy continues to have an impact on the modern Jewish and Muslim communities in Spain and beyond.

The Inquisition's most infamous episode, the expulsion of the Jews from Spain in 1492, was in part a result of Bernat de Puigcercós's efforts to root out the Jewish population. Today, many Jews and Muslims view the Inquisition as a symbol of the dark history of Christian anti-Semitism and Islamophobia.
